name: Connecticut Science & Engineering Fair (CSEF)

aid: Free to enter; special awards and mini-grants (e.g., Urban School Challenge Mini-Grant) available
notes: Strong fit for biology research projects; 2027 fair fully remote (judging via Zoom); CSEF is the CT pathway to major national science competitions.

name: Connecticut High School Science and Humanities Symposium (CT HSSHS, formerly CT JSHS)
deadline: 2027 date TBD (2026 symposium was Feb 28); registration info typically posted by mid-November - check ctjshs.com
eligibility: CT high school students in grades 9-12 with original STEM research
cost: Free (no attendance fee)
aid: Free; no fee
notes: Federal JSHS program is suspended, but CT AHEC runs its own nearly identical symposium; 2026 top finishers advanced to the Interregional JSHS. Watch ctjshs.com in Nov 2026 for 2027 registration.

name: Yale Pathways to Science
deadline: Teacher nominations in spring; Scholar applications in June; decisions announced late August
eligibility: Students entering grades 6-12 in New Haven, West Haven, and Orange/Amity public schools
cost: Free
aid: Free - all programming at no cost
notes: Highest-value Yale exposure for CT students if district-eligible (free research experiences at Yale labs, summer research placements for qualifying juniors/seniors); email yalepathways@yale.edu with questions.

name: NE FIRST / Connecticut FIRST Robotics (FRC)
deadline: FRC 2027 season team registration typically opens ~Sept 2026; build season starts Jan 2027; regional competitions Mar-Apr 2027
eligibility: CT high school students (grades 9-12) via a school or community FRC team
cost: Team-dependent (team fees/fundraising; typically a few hundred dollars per student or less with team fundraising)
aid: FIRST offers rookie grants, fundraising tools, and financial aid; many CT teams fully subsidize student costs
notes: Strong STEM + leadership resume builder; CT has many active FRC teams; start team conversations in September 2026 for the 2027 season.

name: UConn Early College Experience (ECE)
deadline: Enrollment through your high school each semester; spring-course registration typically Oct-Feb (drop deadlines ~Oct 16 / Feb 6)
eligibility: CT high school students at UConn ECE partner high schools
cost: $50 per course credit (e.g., $150 for a 3-credit course)
aid: Full program-fee waiver for students eligible for free/reduced-price meals or categorically eligible (SNAP/TANF); need-based reductions for private school students
notes: Excellent way to build a college biology transcript in 11th grade; credit transfers to UConn and most colleges; also sponsors CT Science Olympiad.

name: Connecticut Science Olympiad (CTSO)
deadline: Team registration typically fall 2026; state tournament ~March 2027 (2026 was Mar 14)
eligibility: CT high school students via school teams (up to 15 members per team, 2 teams per school)
cost: School/team registration fee (varies, nominal)
aid: Low-cost team event; schools typically cover fees
notes: Strong biology fit (events like Disease Detectives, Anatomy & Physiology); only CT qualifier for Science Olympiad Nationals.

name: Connecticut High School Mock Trial Competition (CT Bar Association)
deadline: Team registration typically Sept - Nov (2024-25 registration window was Sep 13 - Nov 10); season runs Dec - Mar
eligibility: CT high school teams (grades 9-12), organized through a school or community group
cost: Nominal team registration fee (pay-later/fee-waiver registration option offered)
aid: Fee waiver / pay-later option available
notes: Perfect fit for a law interest: witness roles, opening/closing statements, objections; state champions advance to national-level competition.

name: Connecticut Envirothon
deadline: Team registration typically opens fall 2026; 2026 Field Day was May 21 (2027 date TBD)
eligibility: CT high school students via 5-person school teams (middle school division also exists)
cost: Minimal team registration fee
aid: Low-cost; schools often cover fees; virtual training content is free
notes: Hands-on environmental science with expert-led workshops - strong biology/environment fit; also offers an annual t-shirt design contest.

name: Connecticut History Day (National History Day CT)
deadline: Registration typically opens fall 2026; state contest ~April-May 2027
eligibility: CT students in grades 6-12
cost: Minimal registration fee
aid: Low-cost; school support typical
notes: Fits law/history interest - students often choose landmark trials, constitutional issues, and civil-rights topics; strong writing/research credential.

name: New England Math Match (NEAML - New England Association of Math Leagues)
deadline: CT state math match ~March 2027; NEAML match late April 2027
eligibility: CT high school math team members; teams qualify via CT leagues and the CT state match (top 2-3 schools per league auto-qualify)
cost: Minimal (school-sponsored)
aid: Low-cost school team activity
notes: Regional math team competition across New England; past NEAML problems/solutions available on ctstatemath.org for practice.

name: PSAT/NMSQT (National Merit Qualifying Test) - October 2026
deadline: 2026-10-17 (school-day window Oct 1-30, 2026; Saturday option Oct 17, 2026; registration is through the high school, so contact the school counselor NOW - school deadlines are typically late Sept/early Oct 2026)
eligibility: U.S. high school students; for National Merit qualification the test must be taken in the student's junior year (2026-27 for Class of 2028)
cost: ~$18 per test (schools often cover or waive this; fee waivers available for eligible students)
aid: N/A (test fee only). Top scorers qualify for National Merit recognition: $2,500 NMSC scholarships and corporate/college-sponsored awards
notes: Test is digital (Bluebook app). CT schools typically administer on a school day in October; check with the school's AP/guidance office about which date and how to register. SAT Suite fee waiver covers the PSAT/NMSQT fee for eligible students. Scores released ~early-mid December 2026.

name: SAT - 2026-27 National Test Dates
deadline: Next deadline: 2026-08-07 (Aug 22 test); then Aug 28 (Sep 12), Sep 18 (Oct 3), Oct 23 (Nov 7), Nov 20 (Dec 5), Feb 19, 2027 (Mar 6), Apr 16, 2027 (May 1), May 21, 2027 (Jun 5). Late registration (~4 days later, +$38) available worldwide.
eligibility: Open to all U.S. high school students; no age or grade restrictions
cost: $68 registration fee (+$38 late registration; +$34 change/cancel fee)
aid: Fee waivers available for eligible low-income students (waives registration, includes 2 free score sends and other benefits)
notes: Digital SAT via Bluebook. Scores typically in ~13 days. Deadlines expire 11:59 p.m. ET. Fall 2027 dates (Aug 28, Sep 18, Oct 2, Nov 6, Dec 4) and spring 2028 dates (Mar 4, May 6, Jun 3) also published for planning. Juniors aiming for early admissions should target a final SAT by spring 2027 or summer 2027.

name: ACT - 2026-27 National Test Dates
deadline: Next deadline: 2026-08-14 (Sep 19 test; late reg until Sep 1 +$42); then Sep 11 (Oct 17; late Sep 29), Nov 6 (Dec 12; late Nov 29), Jan 22, 2027 (Feb 27; late Feb 9), Mar 5, 2027 (Apr 10; late Mar 23), May 7, 2027 (Jun 12; late May 25), Jun 4, 2027 (Jul 10; late Jun 22). eligibility: Open to all U.S. high school students; no age or grade restrictions

CT public school juniors also take the SAT (not ACT) on a state school day in spring; ACT is the private-option alternative. Projected 2027-28 dates (Sep 11, Oct 16, Dec 11, 2027) also published.

name: AP Exams - May 2027 (2027 administration)

eligibility: Students enrolled in (or self-studying) AP courses; registration via the high school's AP coordinator - homeschooled students can arrange testing at a local school that administers AP Exams

CT public schools charge fees per district policy; ask the AP coordinator about total cost and any CT state fee support. AP scores released early July 2027.

name: CLT (Classic Learning Test) - 2026-27 Test Dates
deadline: Next deadlines: 2026-08-13 (Aug 22 remote test); then Sep 10 (Sep 17 remote), Oct 8 (Oct 17 remote), Oct 14 (Nov 14 in-school), Nov 5 (Nov 14 remote), Dec 3 (Dec 8 remote). 2027 dates include Jan 23, Feb 18, Mar 20, Apr 17, May 22, Jun 17 (deadlines ~9-10 days prior).

cost: $112 per test (remotely proctored; in-school pricing set by school)
aid: CLT fee waivers/assistance available for students with financial need (contact CLT); many colleges award merit scholarships based on CLT scores
notes: Good fit for classical/liberal-arts curricula - sections are Verbal Reasoning, Grammar/Writing, Quantitative Reasoning. Verify target colleges accept CLT before choosing it over SAT/ACT. Full 2026-27 date list also available as a downloadable PDF from the CLT site.

name: Connecticut SAT School Day - Spring 2027 (CT public schools)

Check the CT SDE page after Sept 2026 for the exact 2027 date.

deadline: 2026-27 deadlines (per 2025-26 cycle): Dec 30 - team intent-to-compete forms; Dec 31 - independent fencer appeals; Jan 9 - independent fencer registration; Jan 15 - final weapon/squad assignments; Feb 13 - entry forms & payments due. Championships expected early March 2027.

aid: None
notes: State champion titles add a strong regional credential. CHSFA's season runs roughly January-March; check chsfa.org for 2026-27 dates (2026 season was the model above). Contact CHSFAboard@gmail.com for independent fencer questions.

eligibility: USA Fencing members; RJCC = Junior (born 2007+) & Cadet (born 2010+), ROC = open Div I/II/III, RYC = youth age bands; eligibility varies by event
cost: Entry fees typically ~$25-$70 per event (much cheaper than NACs); Competitive or Access membership ($34/$99) plus event fees; local travel only
aid: None
notes: Use fencingcalendar.com and askfred.net to filter Northeast-region events by weapon/age/date; the USA Fencing regional calendar lists all sanctioned events. Candlewood Fencing Center (Newtown/Norwalk, CT - CT's premier club, 111+ hosted tournaments) is the home base to train and find local events. Classification upgrades earned at ROCs/RJCCs directly improve NAC seeding.

cost: $1,450 day camper / $1,700 overnight camper per week (2026 pricing)
aid: None published (need-based programs excluded per profile criteria)
notes: Run by Princeton's fencing staff; focused individual development plus new technique, all weapons. The 2026 PDF schedule (princetonsportscamps.com) confirms exact session structure. Book early - these are among the most competitive university fencing camps in the Northeast corridor.

name: Tim Morehouse Fencing Club Elite Camps (NYC)

cost: Varies by session/length (5-day elite camps typically several hundred dollars; exact pricing on the registration page)
aid: None published
notes: Tim Morehouse is a two-time Olympic saber medalist (2008 silver, 2016 team) and USA Fencing board member; his camps are among the most accessible elite programs for Northeast fencers. Combine with a visit to Candlewood or another home club for year-round continuity.

name: Regeneron Science Talent Search (STS)
deadline: November 5, 2026, 8pm ET (2027 cycle; application period June 1 - Nov 5, 2026). NOTE: this deadline is for the Class of 2027 (current seniors). Class of 2028 applies in fall 2027 for STS 2028.
eligibility: High school seniors in the U.S. (including U.S. citizens studying abroad); also students who have completed high school graduation requirements but have not yet enrolled in college
cost: Free (no application fee)
aid: $3.1M in awards annually; $250,000 top prize; all 40 finalists receive at least $25,000
notes: Requires a full application: original research report, essays, transcript, and recommendations. Roughly 300 of ~2,600 applicants become Scholars (announced Jan 2027 for this cycle); 40 Finalists advance to Finals Week in Washington, D.C. (March 2027). Prestige is extremely high for selective college admissions.

name: National Merit Scholarship Program
deadline: October 2026 (PSAT/NMSQT administered at school during the October testing window - exact date set by the school; registration typically opens in early fall 2026)
eligibility: U.S. high school students who take the PSAT/NMSQT in their junior year (11th grade); must be U.S. citizens or lawful permanent residents intending to become citizens at the earliest opportunity, and enrolled in high school progressing normally toward graduation
cost: Free (no application fee; entry is automatic via the PSAT/NMSQT taken at school)
aid: National Merit $2,500 Scholarships, corporate-sponsored scholarships (up to $10,000), and college-sponsored scholarships; Semifinalist/Finalist status alone is a major admissions credential
notes: No separate application to enter - the PSAT/NMSQT Selection Index determines recognition. About 16,000 Semifinalists (top scorers per state; CT is a competitive state) must submit a detailed application in senior year (essays, activities, school endorsement, confirming SAT scores) to become Finalists. Qualifying scores vary by state.; [DEAD: https://www.nationalmerit.org/]

deadline: September 30, 2026, 5pm ET (2027 cycle, for students graduating in the 2026-27 school year); Phase 1 application opens August 3, 2026
eligibility: High school/home-schooled students in one of the 50 U.S. states, DC, Puerto Rico, or select DoD schools who will graduate during the current academic year (2026-27 for the 2027 cycle); U.S. citizens, nationals, permanent residents, refugees, asylees, Cuban-Haitian entrants, or humanitarian parolees; minimum 3.0 GPA; planning to attend an accredited U.S. post-secondary institution. International students not eligible.
cost: Free (no application fee)
aid: $20,000 per scholar; 150 scholars selected per year; foundation has awarded $90M+ since 1986
notes: Phase 1 is fast - no essays, transcript, or recommendations. About 1% of applicants become Semifinalists (~1,200), then 250 Regional Finalists interview in late Jan/early Feb, and 150 are selected in April. Strong fit for students with community leadership and service impact.

name: Davidson Fellows Scholarship
deadline: 2027 application opens in Fall 2026 (initial eligibility portion should be submitted as early as possible); 2026 deadline was February 18, 2026 11:59pm PT - expect ~mid-February 2027 for the 2027 cycle
eligibility: U.S. citizens residing in the U.S., or U.S. permanent residents residing in the U.S. (or stationed overseas on active U.S. military duty); 18 years or younger as of the application deadline; must have completed a significant piece of work in an eligible category; two-person teams eligible; must attend an awards reception in Washington, D.C.
cost: Free (no application fee)
aid: $100,000, $50,000, or $25,000 scholarships (judges determine level)
notes: Community service projects are NOT accepted, nor are essays about future majors. Two-part application: initial eligibility submission (reviewed in 1-2 business days), then nominator forms and category requirements. All applicants notified on or before July 15. Judges screen for plagiarism and AI-generated content.

name: U.S. Presidential Scholars Program
deadline: Application opens in January and closes in late February of the senior year (2026 cycle applications closed ~late February 2026; for the Class of 2028, expect Jan-Feb 2028)
eligibility: U.S. citizens or legal permanent residents who graduate (receive a diploma) between January and August of the program year; general component: score exceptionally well on the SAT or ACT (tests taken between August of junior year and October of senior year) or be nominated by a Chief State School Officer or partner recognition organization; arts component via arts nomination; CTE component via CSSO nomination
cost: Free (no application fee)
aid: Honorary national recognition - no cash award; Presidential Scholars medallion and Washington, D.C. recognition events
notes: The general component has NO direct application - students are identified from SAT/ACT score reports, so do NOT opt out of score release to College Board/ACT. Students can also be nominated by their state's Chief State School Officer. 2026 semifinalists were announced May 22, 2026.

name: Regeneron International Science and Engineering Fair (ISEF)

cost: Entry is via affiliated fairs; costs vary by fair (many are free or low-cost with small registration fees) - no fee to compete at ISEF itself
aid: More than $7 million in awards and prizes (2026), including top awards up to $75,000 plus many category and special awards
notes: Requires an original research project entered through an affiliated fair - register early because fair deadlines vary by region (CT regional fairs typically occur in early spring). Winning a top award at the local fair earns the invitation to ISEF. Many ISEF finalists also enter Regeneron STS in senior year, so the same project can feed both.
